alignments.note: One substantive rendered by the phrase manner of law; rule 31 heads it on the word carrying the lexeme, manner being the generic the ASV supplies.
הָיָה is present in the possessive clause, so it takes the recasting have itself together with its auxiliary (rule 43).
The possessive לְ; with הָיָה carrying the have, the recasting leaves the preposition no English word (rules 40, 43).
Suffix takes the English subject pronoun of the recast possessive clause (rules 18, 43).

First comparative preposition takes the opening expression as well; each Hebrew member writes its own preposition, so each takes only the English written for it (rule 14). Head on the connective word (rule 24).
Assimilated article token takes the written the (rule 12).
Noun with the supplied for that rule 33 gives the nominal whose relation the ASV states; the comparative preposition already holds its own English word.
Second comparative preposition takes the answering as.
Assimilated article token takes the written the (rule 12).
Noun with its supplied for (rule 33), rendered home born; rule 31's subtraction leaves home as the distinguishing word. Heading on born was the competing reading.
The second יִהְיֶה; the ASV writes one shall have for the whole sentence (rule 22).
Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English, the copula going to the predicate (rule 20).
Predicate name of the verbless clause, taking the construction-supplied copula (rule 20).

review_notes: Ye shall have is placed under rule 43: הָיָה stands in the clause and takes the have, the לְ goes unrepresented, and the suffix takes the subject pronoun.
The two supplied fors are given to their nouns under rule 33, each comparative preposition already holding an English word of its own.
